question_options.question: How would you rate this pack?
Do you know your town history?
Which character did you like the most?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: We need to investigate.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Hey, what about Amanda? Her father is a supervisor at the plant. If Prince Automotive really is shutting down, he'd have to know about it!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Let's go!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I mean, I know that long distance relationships almost never work out, but that doesn't mean we shouldn't try.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: And besides, we've both got email and cell phones and instant messages!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: It'll be just like we're together only...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Only we won't be.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: And sooner or later, you'll break up with me or I'll break up with you. That's how these things always go.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Well, when you put it like that...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Maybe you're ready for me to pack my stuff and move to Michigan, Mallika, but I'm not! Centerscore is my home.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Spike, that's not what I meant! You're my boyfriend. I'm ready to do whatever it takes to keep you here.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Then start acting like it. We need to figure some stuff out.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Like what?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well, if what my mom says is right, the Soup Shack will only be in trouble if Prince Automotive shuts down.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Okay, so...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: So Prince Automotive is the primary source of revenue for the Prince family. Why would Silas Prince deliberately shut it down?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: That's a good question, Spike. And I think I see where you're going with this.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: You think there's more to this than meets the eye.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Exactly... The Flex-Games, the Prince Prix, the Crosstown Races. When has the Prince Family ever done anything on the level?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: You will?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Sure!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I like your attitude, Mallika, but I'm still not sure what we can do.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Well, me either, but I'm positive that sitting here feeling sorry for ourselves won't do us any good.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: You're right, Mallika!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Exactly! Now we just need to figure some things out.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Like what?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Well, if what your mother said is true, the Soup Shack will only be in trouble if Prince Automotive shuts down.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Okay, so...

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: So Prince Automotive is the primary source of revenue for the Prince family. Why would Silas Prince deliberately shut it down?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well, maybe the factory hasn't been doing well. Maybe people don't want to buy Prince cars.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: It's possible, but I doubt it.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: What do you mean?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Think about it... The Flex-Games, the Prince Prix, the Crosstown Races. When has the Prince Family ever done anything on the level?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I'm not sure what Silas Prince is up to just yet, but I'm sure there's more to this than meets the eye.
As Spike leans forward to kiss Mallika, the front door flies open...

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Oh dear, oh dear...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Mom, what's going on? Your shift at the Soup Shack doesn't end for two more hours.

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: I know. I just... Who can even think about work at a time like this?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: A time like what? What's going on?

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: During the lunch rush, I overheard several executives from Prince Automotive talking about the plant.

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: They said Silas Prince intends to shut it down! All of it!

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Prince Automotive is the biggest employer in town. If it goes, all of Main Street will go with it. That means I'll lose my job, and...

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: I know I shouldn't burden you with this, Spike, but I just don't know what to do. Things were finally starting to look up, but now... Now...
Mrs. Chapman crosses into her bedroom and closes the door.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Wow, your mom seems pretty torn up.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: She'll be okay.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Really?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yeah, we're used to having it rough.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: At least, things shouldn't be too bad, right?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Your mom still has all that money you won at the Flex-Games. That should tide your family over until she can find a new job.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yeah.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Spike, what are you not telling me?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Last month, Chip... He cracked a tooth on the playground, and we kinda had to, you know, cover it.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Afterwards, we had a family discussion about money, and...

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: And...?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: And if my mom gets laid off, things could get bad, okay? We might even have to move back East with my grandparents.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: All the way back to Michigan?!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Don't worry, Spike. I'll...

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: More?! Why?!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: To make sure you've memorized how to do these kinds of problems. You do have a test on Thursday, right?

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: Yeah, but... But Spike always lets me play after I finish the assignment. Are you saying you know better than Spike?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Uh, no... That's not what I...

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: So then Spike is right, and you're wrong?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Spike, help!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yo, little bro. Mallika helped you out. Now you're going to game her like that? Uncool!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Apologize to Mallika, and go to your room.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: Sorry, Mallika.
Chip sulks up the stairs.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I don't know what happened, Spike. We were getting along so well, and then...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I know. You were just trying to help, but you're also an only child. Kids need a balance between work and play.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Even so, Chip shouldn't have behaved like that. I'm going to let him stew for a while, then I'll send him outside to burn off all that extra energy.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: And in the meantime...?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yeah?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I mean, we're alone, right?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Oh, right!

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: Awesome! Thanks, Mallika! You're the best!
Chip grabs his books and races outside.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Thanks again for helping Chip with his homework, Mallika. You're way better at explaining this math stuff than I am.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: No problem. And besides, now you owe me one.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Sure. One what?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Well... How about we start with one kiss? And then we'll work from there.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I can live with that!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Are you sure?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I heard Amanda's dad say so.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: That sucks.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Bye, Amanda.
Amanda enters the house and shuts the door. Mallika and Spike hang for an awkward, somber moment. Finally, Mallika speaks...

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I'm sorry, Spike. It looks like the auto plant really will be shutting down.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Good idea, Spike. I'm going to listen in.
Mallika presses her ear to the door.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: It's totally working! I can hear what Amanda's dad is saying!

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: This is unacceptable, Silas! If you shut down the plant, you'll put a lot of decent men and women out of work!

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: And don't try to feed me any of that cash flow malarkey! I've seen the books. Prince Automotive is as profitable today as it's ever been!

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Not to mention the fact that there have been no major safety violations in over fifteen years.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: I know you know that, sir, I just...

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Yes sir, I understand that it was your brother who died in that tragic accident.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Did I hear something about a 'brother'? What's Amanda's dad talking about in there?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Quiet, Spike! Keep it down! We're trying to be sneaky here!
Suddenly, the door swings open! Mallika and Spike topple forward!

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: What exactly do you two kids think you're doing?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I'm sorry, sir, but we...

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: We wanted to ask you a few questions about the rumors we've been hearing about Prince Automotive shutting down.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: I'm sorry, kids. I don't know what you were expecting, but it's the policy of Prince Automotive employees to `never` comment on rumors.
nodes.text_bbcode: I'm sorry, kids. I don't know what you were expecting, but it's the policy of Prince Automotive employees to [i]never[/i] comment on rumors.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Especially to a couple of eavesdropping snoops like you.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: I'll have my daughter escort you out.
Amanda escorts Mallika and Spike out the front door.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: Guys, whatever you asked my dad really made him cranky.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: We're sorry, Amanda.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: It's okay. I'm sure he'll get over it... Someday.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I think we should wait over here, Spike.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: We need information from Amanda's dad. The last thing we'd want to do is make him mad at us.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Oh... Good point.
A few minutes later, the door to the office opens, and Amanda's dad steps out.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Well, hello there. What can I do for you kids?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Sir, we'd heard some rumors floating around about the Prince Automotive plant shutting down, and we were hoping you could tell us if the rumors are true.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Well, Prince Automotive employees aren't supposed to comment on rumors...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Please, sir. My mom works at the Soup Shack, and if the plant closes, she'll lose her job! Can't you tell us anything?

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Grr... See? This is exactly what I told Silas! His actions are affecting everyone!

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: If you kids promise to keep it to yourselves... I'll tell you everything.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: First off, the rumors are true. I just got off the phone with Silas Prince, and I can verify that he does plan to shut down Prince Automotive.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: But for the life of me, I can't figure out why.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Prince Automotive is more profitable right now than it's been in years, and our safety record speaks for itself.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Aside from the unfortunate incident with Silas's brother fifteen years ago, we've never had a major accident.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Silas Prince has a brother?

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: `Had` a brother. The accident was fatal. But that was a long time ago.
nodes.text_bbcode: [i]Had[/i] a brother. The accident was fatal. But that was a long time ago.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Anyway, I'm sorry to be the bearer of such bad news.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: I've got some more phone calls to make. Would you mind if Amanda escorted you out?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Not a problem. And thanks for everything!
Amanda escorts Mallika and Spike out.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: My dad's been pretty worried these last few days. It seems like he was relieved to finally talk to somebody.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: Thanks for coming over!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: No sweat. Glad to be of assistance.
Amanda peeks her head into the bedroom.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: Mallika, Spike! Hi there! When did you get here?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Amanda, you just let us in a second ago.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: Oh goody! I knew I'd forgotten something!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: You seem pretty happy about it.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: I'm glad it was just you. The last time I forgot something, we had to get a new microwave.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: And a new kitchen.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: Anyway, are you here to try on dresses for the Prom, too?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Wait, so that's what Paula was doing? She was trying on dresses for the Prom?!

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: Spike! Shh!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Wait... What?

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: Please don't tell Paula I told you, but Paula's family has been on a money diet ever since she stole the tiara.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Money diet?

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: The school board decided to let Paula attend the Prom, but now she can't afford to buy a new dress, and...
Paula storms back into the bedroom.

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Amanda, what part of 'on the Q.T.' did you not understand?!

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: Um... The part where I was supposed to know what 'Q.T.' meant, I think.

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: It meant 'QUIET TIME'!

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: If I'd wanted the whole school to know why I was here, I would've posted about it on FaceSpace.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Honestly, Paula, we won't tell anybody about your family's money troubles.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: We only came over because we have questions we'd like to ask Amanda's father about Silas Prince.

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Did you say, 'Silas Prince'?!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Yeah, is that a problem?

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: No, it's just... That jerk is the reason I'm over here borrowing... I mean, the reason I'm taking back this dress I let Amanda borrow.

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Silas Prince forced my father to sign over all of our property in exchange for not pressing charges against me. Now my family is... Is... Poor!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Not having money isn't the end of the world, Paula.

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Maybe not for you. You're used to it! But me... My world is over. Look at me! I used to wear Versaze. Now I wear Ver-sucky!
Paula turns and flees to the restroom once again.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: I think I should go give Paula a hug. If you still want to talk to my dad, he's in his office.
A few moments later, Spike and Mallika step up to the office door.
From within, they hear one half of a heated conversation.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Hey... It sounds like Amanda's dad is arguing with somebody. He could be talking about the plant. Maybe we should listen in.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Hm. Eavesdropping isn't exactly the polite thing to do, but if Amanda's dad is talking about the plant, we might get some juicy intel. I should...

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Yeah, Spike, girls get dressed up all the time.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: But you never...

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Sure, I do. Just not when you're around.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Oh. Cool. And now that I think about it, there are plenty of things I do when you're not around too.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Like dancing around in my underwear to Rhianna Louisianna singles.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Really?! You do that?!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I mean... Sure, just like that.

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Anyway, I think I've had enough dress up fun for today. I'm going to change back into my street clothes. Later, haters.
As Paula steps toward the bathroom, she glances to Mallika and whispers...

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Oh, and Mallika, thanks for backing me up.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Uh, you're kidding, right? I'm all for dressing up for a school dance, but I would never hang out in a dress with a corset just for fun.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I consider breathing a top priority.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: And now that I think about it, didn't I see Amanda wear that dress to the Homecoming Dance last year?

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: No, I mean... Don't be silly! My family is rich! Like I'd ever wear somebody else's dress!

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: This dress is... Well, it's a lot like that dress you remember, but by a totally different and much more expensive designer and... And...

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Mallika, I hate you! And the video you made of the senior fashion show was amateurish at best!
Paula spins on her heels and rushes into the bathroom.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Whoa, what did you say?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Whatever it was, it was definitely the wrong thing.
Thirty minutes later, Mallika and Spike stand outside Amanda's house. Mallika presses the doorbell.
From inside, there comes a frantic shuffling sound. The door swings open!

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Mallika! Spike! Did you see it?

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Uh... See what?

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Whatever made that ringing sound! I've been trying to track it down for weeks, but it always seems to disappear right before I open the door.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Amanda, are you talking about the doorbell?

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: So you have seen it!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Um... Amanda, we're not here about that. Can we come in?

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: Oh! Of course.
Mallika and Spike enter Amanda's house. Before following them in, Amanda hangs in the doorway, her eyes scanning the empty street.

nodes.speaker: Mr. Doom
nodes.text: I'll find you, ringybird... Some day...
Mallika and Spike enter Amanda's bedroom. Paula stands by the bed.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Paula!

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Mallika, Spike, what are you two doing here?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: We just dropped by to ask Amanda's dad a few questions and... Paula, are you wearing an evening gown?

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Yeah, it's... It's just something we girls do from time to time.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Really?

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Yeah! I mean, we girls totally like to dress up and enjoy the feel of silky fabric on our skin. Right, Mallika?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Not that I'd expect a skater like you to understand, Spike. Your jeans have more holes than my fishnets.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Hey!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Hm, dressing up is definitely not something I do, but Paula seems pretty uncomfortable with this line of questioning. Maybe I should back her up.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Regardless, we should check in on Brendan and Dinah. Hopefully, they'll be able to tell us why somebody thought we should have this journal so badly.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Sure. Let's go... Um...

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Spike, what are you waiting for?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Did you hear that?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Yeah. It sounds like the wind... Only way creepier. And it's almost like it's saying something. A word. 'Tomb'? 'Room'?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Mallika, not a whole lot scares me, but I think we should get out of here.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: No argument from me.
As Mallika and Spike exit the parking lot, a pale, gaunt figure emerges from the deep shadows.

nodes.speaker: Janitor
nodes.text: doooooooooooooom.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Wild Woodsman?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Yeah, he's one of the `local ghosts` of Centerscore. Brendan and Dinah wrote an article about him for the school newspaper.
nodes.text_bbcode: Yeah, he's one of the [i]local ghosts[/i] of Centerscore. Brendan and Dinah wrote an article about him for the school newspaper.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I remember that! And it turned out that the Wild Woodsman wasn't so wild, right?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Exactly! His real name was Jonah Prez, and he was actually a devoted family man. Brendan and Dinah discovered that he was murdered by the scofflaw Obadiah Prince.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Any relation?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: A guy named 'Prince' with a penchant for misbehavior. What do you think?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Anyway, over the years, the story got reversed. People now remember Jonah Prez as the bandit and Obadiah Prince as the town hero.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: That's pretty crazy. How do you rewrite history like that?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I'm not sure.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: The town founder?!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Wait... Wasn't he?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: No! The town founders were the Brothers Centerscore, remember?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Oh, that's right. Ollie, Late, and Winston. I've never been good at local history. Then who is Jonah Prez?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: He was... Oh, that's right! He's the Wild Woodsman! Brendan and Dinah wrote an article about him for the school newspaper.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: But isn't the Wild Woodsman a ghost?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Sure, he's a ghost now, but ghosts were living, breathing people once. Jonah Prez must've written this before he died.

nodes.speaker: Dinah
nodes.text: Silas Prince made an offer on the bakery.

nodes.speaker: Dinah
nodes.text: I told him no, but now he's sending lawyers here to try to convince me that selling would be in my 'best interest'.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Wait... Silas Prince wants to buy the bakery?

nodes.speaker: Dinah
nodes.text: No, not just the bakery! As far as I can tell, he's made an offer on nearly every property on Main Street. He's practically buying up the whole town!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Whoa...

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Closing the plant for no reason is one thing, and buying up real estate is another. But doing both at the same time, that's really suspicious.

nodes.speaker: Dinah
nodes.text: Silas Prince is closing Prince Automotive? But all the businesses around here depend on the money they make off the plant employees.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: We know, Kim. And we also know that Silas Prince is up to something devious.

nodes.speaker: Dinah
nodes.text: But what exactly?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: We're not sure yet. But Kim, I promise you... Spike and I will find out. And if there's anything we can do to help you and the bakery out, we'll do it.

nodes.speaker: Dinah
nodes.text: Thanks, guys.
Mallika and Spike cross through the parking lot to Mallika's car. As they near the vehicle, Spike races forward!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: No way! So uncool!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Spike, what is it?!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Look, somebody busted out your passenger side window.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: On no! Did they take anything?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Nope. Stereo is still here, so is all of your film equipment, but...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Weird. I think whoever broke into your car left something on the seat for you.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: What? Who breaks into a car and `leaves` something? That's like bizarro-stealing.
nodes.text_bbcode: What? Who breaks into a car and [i]leaves[/i] something? That's like bizarro-stealing.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I don't know who did it, but check this out. It's a book, and it looks really old.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Whoa! Feel that leather? It's super brittle. This book isn't just old, it's ancient.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I'm going to open it.
Mallika opens the book to the inscription page.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Hm... The inscription says that this book is the journal of Jonah Prez, and the first entry is dated August of 1863.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: 'Jonah Prez'? Does that name sound familiar to you?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Yeah! Jonah Prez was the...

nodes.speaker: Dinah
nodes.text: You think just because I'm talking to a lawyer, `I` did something wrong?
nodes.text_bbcode: You think just because I'm talking to a lawyer, [i]I[/i] did something wrong?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: No, it isn't that. I just...

nodes.speaker: Dinah
nodes.text: You just what?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Well, you are known for diss battling, and some of those other diss battlers get into trouble from time to time, so...

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: You know, I assumed.

nodes.speaker: Dinah
nodes.text: Wow, Mallika. Thanks for the vote of no confidence. I thought we were friends.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: We are!

nodes.speaker: Dinah
nodes.text: Sure, you just wouldn't leave me alone with your handbag.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Uh, Mallika, maybe you should let me handle this.

nodes.speaker: Spike

nodes.text: Blue diamonds, actually.

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: Pretty and rare, yes, but also of an exceedingly high thermal conductivity, making them invaluable for nanoscopic fabrication processes.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Invaluable? So are the diamonds worth something or not?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Spike, invaluable means more than valuable.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Oh, right. Just like how the rapper Inglorious L.A.R.G.E. is 'infamous'.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Forget it, Spike.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Silas, we know all about your plan to close Prince Automotive and buy up the town!

nodes.text: You do?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yeah!

nodes.text: Well, I suppose that's only fitting. You see, the irony here is that I have you and your friends to thank for this discovery.

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: It all began with an article I read in your school newspaper...

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: Tom! What did I tell you about leaving newspapers all around the...

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: Wait! What is this...?

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: The article revealed a truth about my family even I hadn't known.

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: No, it can't be! My great-great-grandfather Obadiah... No better than a common thief!

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: Digging deeper into my ancestor's past, I discovered Obadiah made his fortune from a secret diamond mine he'd murdered Jonah Prez to acquire.
Rumor says you found something, you varmint, and I want it.

nodes.speaker: Candy
nodes.text: Obadiah, please don't hurt me! I'll give you anything...

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: But like all criminals, Obadiah was a superstitious and cowardly individual. He feared he would suffer the same bloody fate as Jonah Prez.

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: So to preserve the secrets of the diamond mine, Obadiah constructed a building over the mine entrance. Something he was sure would avert all suspicion.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Oh my gosh! Obadiah built the old orphanage!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: But aren't we in a library?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Sure, now... But a hundred years ago, Wilson High was a home for displaced children.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: That's right! Judge Tigh told a story about that at the beginning of the Crosstown Races. Obadiah brought medicine to the kids who lived here.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: But it wasn't just medicine Obadiah brought, was it? He was checking up on his diamonds.

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: Precisely!

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: It was a brilliant plan... Or it should've been. You see, Obadiah never told his heirs about the concealed diamond mine.

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: And after he mysteriously disappeared, the secret was lost to time.

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: Until I rediscovered it, that is.

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: Hm... According to my calculations, the diamond mine should be right... `HERE!`

nodes.text: And once I knew where it was, it was a simple matter to encourage my son to burn down the old library.

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: Are you really going to allow those cretins at Centerscore to defeat Spartan Academy at an event celebrating the memory of your own ancestor?

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: But... But what can I do?

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: I think `I` have an idea.

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: And from here, I learned the truth... There are clusters of diamonds stretched beneath all of Centerscore, diamonds worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: Diamonds worth even more than Prince Automotive!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: But to get at the diamonds, you needed to own property... Lots of it.

nodes.speaker: Spike

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: YES!!! And then after I've bought the land, I'll raze the buildings, and extract the diamonds from beneath their foundations!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: There's only one problem, Silas. Once people find out about the diamonds, they'll never sell to you.

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: You have a cunning mind, Mallika. I knew as much when you created that documentary about me during the Prince Prix.

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: But let me ask you a question. How will you tell anybody about my schemes... From in there?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: What do you mean, 'in there'?

nodes.speaker: Jonah Prez
nodes.text: I mean, 'IN THERE'!!!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
